sections.title: Tangent to a Parabola
sections.content: For y² = 4ax: Point form (at x1,y1) is yy1 = 2a(x+x1). Slope form is y = mx + a/m (point of contact is a/m², 2a/m). Parametric form is ty = x + at².

sections.title: Tangent to Ellipse and Hyperbola
sections.content: Ellipse slope form: y = mx ± √(a²m² + b²). Hyperbola slope form: y = mx ± √(a²m² - b²). The 'T = 0' rule applies for the point form for all conics.

sections.title: Director Circle
sections.content: The locus of the intersection of perpendicular tangents. For Parabola: It is the directrix (x = -a). For Ellipse: x² + y² = a² + b². For Hyperbola: x² + y² = a² - b².

sections.title: Normals to a Parabola
sections.content: For y² = 4ax: Slope form is y = mx - 2am - am³ (point of contact is am², -2am). Parametric form is y = -tx + 2at + at³. At most three normals can be drawn from a point to a parabola.

sections.title: Normals to Ellipse and Hyperbola
sections.content: Ellipse point form: (a²x/x1) - (b²y/y1) = a² - b². Hyperbola point form: (a²x/x1) + (b²y/y1) = a² + b². Parametric normal for ellipse: ax secθ - by cscθ = a² - b².

sections.title: Chord of Contact and T=S1
sections.content: Chord of contact from external point (x1, y1) to any conic is T = 0. The equation of a chord whose midpoint is (x1, y1) is T = S1.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Using y = mx - a/m instead of y = mx + a/m for parabola tangent.
2) Confusing the director circle of a hyperbola (a² - b²) with the ellipse (a² + b²). If b² > a² in a hyperbola, the director circle does not exist (no real perpendicular tangents).
3) Forgetting that the parameter 't' in parabola normal is t = -m.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 is algebraically intensive. Memorize the tangent and normal equations in slope and parametric forms. Know the Director Circle loci and how to manipulate T=0 and T=S1.

tricks.title: Focal Chord Extremities
tricks.explanation: If (at1², 2at1) and (at2², 2at2) are endpoints of a focal chord of a parabola, then t1 * t2 = -1.
tricks.example: If one end is t=2, the other end is instantly t = -1/2.

tricks.title: Intersection of Tangents (Parabola)
tricks.explanation: Tangents at t1 and t2 on y²=4ax intersect at the Geometric Mean of x-coordinates and Arithmetic Mean of y-coordinates.

tricks.title: Condition of Tangency (c values)
tricks.explanation: Memorize 'c' for y=mx+c to be a tangent. Parabola: c = a/m. Ellipse: c² = a²m² + b². Hyperbola: c² = a²m² - b².
tricks.example: For y=2x+c to touch x²/16 + y²/9 = 1, c² = 16(4) + 9 = 73 → c = ±√73.

tricks.title: Reflection Property of Parabola
tricks.explanation: Any ray parallel to the axis of a parabola will pass exactly through the focus after reflection. Conversely, a light source at the focus produces a parallel beam.
tricks.example: Used to find the equation of a reflected ray without calculating angles of incidence/reflection.

tricks.title: Orthogonal Tangents on Directrix
tricks.explanation: Any two tangents drawn to a parabola from a point on its directrix are ALWAYS perpendicular. Their chord of contact is ALWAYS a focal chord.
tricks.example: If asked for the angle between tangents from (-a, 5), it's instantly 90°.

tricks.title: Three Normals Condition
tricks.explanation: For y²=4ax, 3 real normals can be drawn from (h,k) only if h > 2a. The sum of the slopes of the three normals is always 0 (m1+m2+m3=0).
tricks.example: If two normals have slopes 2 and 3, the third normal must have slope -5.
